gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the "0.125 ms latency" these makers print is the 8,000 Hz report interval (1 ÷ 8,000 s), so it holds only in a mode that keeps 8,000 Hz; nor that Gamakay's blog claims 8K "Wireless & Wired" for the TK75HE V2, against the 8,000 Hz wired / 1,000 Hz wireless ChatGPT quoted for Attack Shark.
standout_why: I could not open any cited rival page today: attackshark.com, gamakay.com and keychron.com product pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt (including a delayed background retry of four pages, which all failed), and attackshark.ca failed on a certificate error. The comparison is therefore against what ChatGPT's two answers quote from the Attack Shark X65 Pro HE and X68 Pro HE pages (8,000 Hz wired, 1,000 Hz wireless), so rivals already hold the headline drop. What they appear to lack is a per-mode table across makers and the note that 0.125 ms is arithmetic, not a measurement. The Gamakay 8K-wireless claim comes from a blog bullet that does not separate 2.4 GHz from Bluetooth; it would rate 2 to 3 only once the product page or manual confirms it per mode. The Aula Hero75 HE, HESVAP (Best Buy) and manuals.plus results were not opened.
decides: If Gamakay's product page confirms 8,000 Hz over 2.4 GHz, the TK75HE V2 (which we link) wins the question over the Attack Shark boards ChatGPT named, because it would keep rapid trigger and the full polling rate off the cable. On today's evidence this is a lead, not a settled pick: no page I opened says in words that rapid trigger stays active on 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth for any candidate.
